chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Marwan, from Ammar ibn Musa, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What do you say about a group of people who were traveling and walking on the shore of the sea, when they found a dead man naked whom the sea had cast up? They were naked themselves and had nothing on them except an izar (waistcloth). How do they pray over him while he is naked, and they do not have a surplus garment to shroud him in? He (peace be upon him) said: 'A grave is dug for him and he is placed in his grave (lahd), and the brick is placed over his private parts, so his private parts are covered by the brick and the stone. Then prayer is performed over him, and then he is buried.' I said: 'So prayer is not performed over him after he is buried?' He said: 'Prayer is not performed over the dead after he is buried, nor is prayer performed over him while he is naked until his private parts are covered.'

key_terms.عَوْرَة: Private parts (awrah) that must be covered
key_terms.لَحْد: A grave with a niche or recess on one side
key_terms.يُكَفِّنُونَهُ: To shroud him (in the burial cloth)

ai.seo_question: How is funeral prayer performed if the corpse is naked and no shroud is available?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural priority of covering the *awrah* (private parts) before performing the funeral prayer, even in emergency situations where no cloth is available. It establishes that the prayer is not performed over the grave after burial, reinforcing the standard practice of praying before interment, and highlights the flexibility of using available materials like bricks or stones to ensure modesty during the ritual.
